subject: Erasures sampling & export choreography for third-party audit
messages:
From: Tim Wells <tim.wells@clearwavebank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: audit@cg-auditors.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Request: erasure sampling plan + sample export for audit

Hi Soojin,

We are preparing for our independent SOC2 refresh and CG Auditors asked for a short window of evidence focused on tenant erasures (data deletions). Specifically they want: 
- A brief description of the sampling methodology used when validating tenant deletions (how samples are selected, size, and periodicity).
- A redacted sample export showing the tenant id, deletion timestamp, and deletion method (soft vs hard), plus any retention TTL metadata.
- A short chain-of-custody note describing how deletion requests are tracked through the stack (api -> job -> infra) so they can map events to artifacts.

Can you provide the artifacts or point me to where they live? Tim (audit@cg-auditors.com) is included for coordination. Ideally we can hand over the items by end of week.

Thanks,
Tim
Head of Cloud Risk
ClearWave Bank
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tim Wells <tim.wells@clearwavebank.com>, audit@cg-auditors.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: erasure sampling plan + sample export for audit

Hi Tim —

Thanks for the clear ask. I pulled together a short sampling plan and a small redacted export that should meet CG's needs. High level: 
- Sampling: stratified across geozone and tenant size buckets (small/med/large). We sample 0.5% of tenant deletions per month with a minimum of 5 tenants per bucket; for audit spot checks we can increase to 2% for the requested month.
- Export fields included: tenant_id (hashed), deletion_ts (ISO8601 UTC), deletion_type (api_request/ttl_job/admin_hard_delete), retention_policy_id, region, and a boolean flag if KV cache purge was executed.
- Chain-of-custody: each deletion request is assigned a deletion_job_id; the deletion_job_id is present in the API request logs, in the job scheduler event, and in the deletion execution trace we persist to our deletion-audit index for 90 days.

I'm attaching: erasure-sampling-plan-v1.pdf (short doc), export-sample-20261128.csv (redacted), coc-token-deletion-snippet.txt (log snippet showing job id mapping).

If CG needs larger sampling or raw tenant ids for correlation with ClearWave records we can arrange an encrypted transfer and a one-time keyshare.

Best,
Soojin
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: erasure sampling plan + sample export for audit

Vivek/Naomi —

FYI ClearWave has requested the sampling plan and a redacted export. I attached the current version. Two open questions before I hand off the export to the auditors: 
1) Does the export include a region-residency mapping that distinguishes EU geozone tenants (we need to confirm any additional retention obligations)?
2) For the chain-of-custody note: can we confirm retention of the deletion-audit index is 90 days across Dedicated and Private deployments or if there are per-tenant exceptions?

Marissa, tagging you because this may be relevant for the SOC2 artifact binder (we should file the sampling plan under Evidence > Data Lifecycle > Erasure).

Thanks — Soojin
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: erasure sampling plan + sample export for audit

Soojin — quick answers: 
1) The export includes a region code (us, eu, apac) and we map region->data_residency in the retention_policy table. For EU tenants we keep additional mapping to physical geozone id; I'll add a short CSV export of the mapping if auditors want it.
2) Deletion-audit index retention is 90 days by default for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private customers the retention window is configurable; we document exceptions in the tenancy onboarding note and we honor customer-specified retention boundaries.

I'll prep the region mapping CSV and hand it to you. Naomi — can you confirm the retention policy text we should include in the chain-of-custody note? The auditors will want a plain English statement of where artifacts live and for how long.

— Vivek
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: erasure sampling plan + sample export for audit

Soojin/Vivek —

Confirming language for chain-of-custody (you can paste this into the note):
"Redwood Inference assigns a unique deletion_job_id to each deletion request. That id is recorded in (a) API access logs, (b) the asynchronous deletion job scheduler, and (c) the deletion-audit index which records the final outcome and artifacts produced during deletion. For Hosted and Dedicated customers, the deletion-audit index is retained for 90 days; for Private deployments the retention is controlled by the customer and documented in onboarding artifacts. Access to deletion-audit artifacts is limited to on-call engineers and the security operations team via RBAC and logged in our access audit. All deletion exports provided to auditors are redacted to remove tenant-identifying metadata and delivered over an encrypted transfer mechanism."

I'll also add a line about TTL enforcement: "TTL-triggered deletions are performed by scheduled jobs which record both the trigger_ts and executed_ts; both fields are included in audit exports where available."

Marissa — feel free to drop this into the evidence binder.

— Naomi
From: audit@cg-auditors.com <audit@cg-auditors.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Tim Wells <tim.wells@clearwavebank.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: erasure sampling plan + sample export for audit

Thanks Soojin — we received the attachments. A couple of follow-ups: 
- Can you provide the region mapping CSV Vivek mentioned so we can confirm EU-residency samples?
- For the deletion_job_id, can you include one example where the tenant had both a TTL-triggered deletion and an API hard-delete for the same tenant id (redacted) so we can verify reconciliation across logs? A single joined sample row is fine.

If you can get those two items by EOD Monday we'll be able to close this portion of the evidence request.

Regards,
CG Audit Team
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: audit@cg-auditors.com, Tim Wells <tim.wells@clearwavebank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: erasure sampling plan + sample export for audit

Audit team —

Attached: region-mapping-20261128.csv and joined-example-redacted.csv which contains a single reconciled row showing a TTL-triggered deletion and a subsequent API hard-delete for the same redacted tenant hash. We used the encrypted SFTP drop configured for ClearWave.

Let me know if you'd like a short handover call to walk through columns. We'll also add these files to the SOC2 evidence binder with retention notes as Naomi drafted.

Best,
Soojin
(Attachments referenced: erasure-sampling-plan-v1.pdf [application/pdf], export-sample-20261128.csv [text/csv], coc-token-deletion-snippet.txt [text/plain], region-mapping-20261128.csv [text/csv], joined-example-redacted.csv [text/csv])
